name: Abadi
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Morea, Oa & Paul, Ma'oni 2013. Tentative Grammar Description for the Gabadi language spoken in Central Province ('Writing systems and sounds'). SIL International; also Kassell & Potter 2011 SIL ESR 2011-030.
earlier_scan.note: SIL PNG sketch plausibly has a sounds/stress section; sil.org could not be reached by automated download and the archived ESR PDF 404s.

sources.citation: Oa, Morea & Ma'oni Paul. 2013. Tentative Grammar Description for the Gabadi Language. Ukarumpa: SIL-PNG ms. (Discover Your Language workshop), 40 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives 56178.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Sec. 2 'Writing system and sounds' (p.7) is only an alphabet list, consonant list (b d g k m n p r s t v ') and vowel list (a e i o u); no statement on word stress anywhere (the word 'stress' occurs only in sec. 8.2 Focus, meaning sentence emphasis). Dialect: Koupuana village.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. Field notebook RB2-004 (pp. 73-133 Gabadi, speaker Rarai Aku). Kaipuleohone, University of Hawai'i.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Open-access handwritten elicitation notes by a phonologically careful fieldworker; may mark stress on Gabadi forms (data, not a statement).

sources.citation: Kassell, Alison & Margaret Potter. 2011. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Abadi Language Group. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011-030. 94 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 8.1 'Characteristics of the language' (pp.30-31) gives consonant and vowel phone charts, free-variation notes and SOV order; nothing on stress; the four-village IPA wordlists in Appendix A carry no stress marks. Its references cite Tauberschmidt & Onken 1999 'Organized phonology data: Abadi' (ms.).

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of Western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Gabadi appears only in cognate sets and sound-correspondence tables; no Gabadi stress statement.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew. 1975. The relationships of the Austronesian languages of Central Papua: a preliminary study. In T.E. Dutton (ed.), Studies in languages of Central and South-East Papua, 3-105. Pacific Linguistics C-29.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.5 Gabadi gives location and informant (Pinu) only; the comparative-phonology sections contain no stress statement for any language.

sources.citation: Strong, W. Mersh. 1912. Note on the Language of Kabadi, British New Guinea. Anthropos 7: 155-160.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Grammar notes only (gender, number/possessive suffixes, pronouns, verbs); no phonology and no accent statement.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1907. Reports of the Cambridge Anthropological Expedition to Torres Straits, vol. III: Linguistics. Cambridge University Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kabadi cited in the comparative phonology/grammar of British New Guinea Melanesian languages (sound correspondences, pronouns); no accent statement for Kabadi.

sources.citation: Tauberschmidt, Gerhard & Mark Onken. 1999. Organized phonology data: Abadi [kbt]. Manuscript. Ukarumpa: SIL-PNG.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: SIL-PNG OPDs have a fixed 'Suprasegmentals/stress' rubric; this is the only known phonological description of Abadi and almost certainly states the stress rule. Cited by Kassell & Potter 2011; not in the public SIL archive listing as of 2016 — request from SIL-PNG Ukarumpa library / SIL Language & Culture Archives (check current pnglanguages.sil.org kbt page, which is could not be reached by automated download).

sources.citation: Rueck, Michael J; Olo'a, Ume; Sam, Deisy; Tapa, Ali; Ure, Kere. 2003. Lala and Gabadi Wordlist 2003 (SIL archives 58433) and Abadi Survey Word List 2003 (SIL archives 56501). SIL International.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: SIL-PNG standard survey wordlists are transcribed in IPA usually with primary-stress marks; would allow the stress pattern to be read off ~170 items x 4 villages even without a prose statement.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. 1943. The linguistic position of South-Eastern Papua. Sydney: Australasian Medical Publishing Co. (Kabadi treated over c. 16 pp.)

sources.note: Glottolog's second-ranked descriptive source for Kabadi (phonology or text collection); Capell routinely notes accent placement in his phonetic remarks on each language group (Western Motu group: Kabadi, Doura, Nara, Roro, Mekeo, Kuni).
